summary: Piscataquis County station from 1913; steel tower completed 1918; removed between 1996 and 2003. The station site is now part of Baxter State Park, and no source describes remains on the summit.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower was removed between 1996 and 2003; no source found describes remains on the summit today

access.note: Summit reached by hiking trails in Baxter State Park from Nesowadnehunk Field or Kidney Pond; no source describes access to any tower remains

visit.trail_note: Nesowadnehunk Field route is the one Baxter State Park rangers typically recommend (mymaine.org guide)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1917 report quoted on Forest Lookouts gives a 48-foot steel tower; the 1920 inventory on the same page gives 24 feet. The sources disagree, so height is left out of facts.

notes_for_editor: Brief record (gone, FFLOS US 105, ME 31, registered 2008) matches. Spelling differs by source: Double Top (Digital Maine, Forest Lookouts) and Doubletop (FFLOS). The removal date is a range in the register; the 1996 event year is only the start of that range. Park status comes from a rare-map dealer's description of the 1919 station, not from a Baxter State Park page; no Baxter source was read. A Facebook post from the FFLA Maine chapter (seen in search results) says a 1972 photo showed the tower inside Baxter State Park with its cab long off, and a 1997 reference to a color photo; the Facebook pages returned only a login shell, so neither claim is used. Those are leads to check. No photos added.
